title: Wedding photographer demo: choose the look
question: The roll picked Contact Sheet. Keep it, take another card, or re-roll.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: a photographer's darkroom proof sheets: film strips laid on a lightbox, frames ringed in red grease pencil
options.thesis: Every wedding is a proof sheet the photographer has already marked: the best frames are circled in red, and you see the choosing, not just the photos.
materials: red grease pencil on a lightbox
options.viewport: A lit contact sheet of one barat in strips of six; three frames are circled in red, and one of them is pulled up full size beside the photographer's name and the next free wedding dates.
options.risk: Can feel cold and technical for something as warm as a wedding if the frames are small and the colour stays black and white.

raised.raise: The red grease pencil is the one hand-made layer: circles and arrows draw themselves onto the best frames as you scroll.
Frame numbers and dates sit in fixed positions like film edge print, so counts read the same everywhere.
One number is set at monumental scale: how many dates are still free this wedding season.
A date is plainly free, one function left, or booked, never a vague maybe.
Feeling lives in the captions; prices, dates and what is included are set in a plain working voice.

options.label: Wedding Album
options.lineage: the bound Pakistani wedding album: velvet cover, gold foil names, thick pages turned one spread at a time
options.thesis: The website as the album the couple will receive: each wedding opens spread by spread, function by function.
options.viewport: A velvet album cover with the photographer's name in gold foil opens onto a mehndi spread.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a wedding photographer; it can look like every other wedding site.

options.label: Lantern River
options.lineage: a night market's river of lanterns and hand-painted stall signs
options.thesis: A wedding night lit by strings of lights: each function (mehndi, barat, walima) is its own lit street to walk down.
options.viewport: A dark street of lights with three painted signs: Mehndi, Barat, Walima, each leading into its photos.
options.case: Holds audience identification (Pakistani weddings are lit at night), but a market reads as shopping, not a photographer's eye.
options.risk: Busy and dark; the photos compete with the lights.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: The photographer explains the wedding day in doodles and comic panels.
options.viewport: A doodled timeline of the wedding day with photos stuck on.
options.case: Fuses poorly: doodles shrink the photos and make the work look casual.
options.kept: One hand-made layer that draws itself on.
options.risk: Playful where couples want to trust the work.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Dates and prices as glowing orange digits.
options.viewport: A bank of glowing digits counting free dates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a lab instrument has nothing to do with a wedding.

options.label: Command Wall
options.thesis: The wedding season as an alarm wall with countdowns.
options.viewport: A giant countdown to the wedding date.
options.case: Fuses poorly: alarm and crisis are the wrong feelings for a wedding.

options.label: Tension Column
options.lineage: tensegrity sculpture of rods and cord
options.viewport: A floating column of rods with package names on cords.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract engineering hides what the couple buys.

options.label: Sleeping City
options.lineage: a surreal city folded like a quilt at night
options.thesis: Each wedding as a dreaming district under one night sky.
options.viewport: A folded night city map with weddings as districts.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dreamy maps slow down browsing the photos.
options.kept: A plain waking voice for the practical notes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark, minimal photographer portfolio, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A full-screen slideshow of wedding photos with the photographer's name in a thin serif.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other photographer site.
